name: Cave In
label: Hydra Head
lede: Four Methuen kids who turned metallic hardcore into space rock, took a major-label detour, went back to their hometown label, and kept making records.

eras.title: Named after a Codeine song
eras.text: Methuen, Massachusetts teenagers with a hardcore record collection and a taste for slower, stranger music. They pick up a name, a label in Aaron Turner's Hydra Head, and their first singer walks out the door.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cave In · Wikipedia: Stephen Brodsky
years.h: [[Stephen Brodsky|a0ff602c-7f3e-472d-8786-953da6cd7591]] and Jay Frechette start Cave In in Methuen
years.p: Frechette sings, Brodsky plays guitar, [[Adam McGrath|489a27df-e1c7-442d-b25b-067a950b7a5b]] plays second guitar, [[John-Robert Conners|5665286e-b278-4453-9636-c495412a8b24]] drums and Justin Matthes plays bass. The name comes from a song by the slowcore band Codeine.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists the original five as Frechette, Brodsky, McGrath, Conners and Matthes, with Andy Kyte briefly replacing Matthes. The name is borrowed from Codeine's "Cave-In," from the album Frigid Stars.

Before the demos and split 7-inches with Gambit, Piebald and Early Grace, Brodsky had already played in a middle-school band called Parasite and in Kid Kilowatt with McGrath and [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]], per Wikipedia.

years.h: First self-titled 7-inch comes out on Hydra Head Records
years.p: It is the band's first official release, on the label run by [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] of [[Isis|5e521e8c-0ab2-44c4-8fd8-14d8d3321265]]. The demos and split 7-inches with Gambit, Piebald and Early Grace came before it.

years.h: Frechette leaves mid-tour for Ten Yard Fight; Dave Scrod steps in
years.p: A three-week East Coast run with [[Morning Again|1b4e059e-856e-49a8-b7ca-c3ee67dcde23]] and Bird of Ill Omen is cut short when Jay Frechette joins [[Ten Yard Fight|c051f242-5907-42ce-b25f-678f14323dac]] full-time. Dave Scrod takes over vocals.

eras.title: Two singers out, one bassist in
eras.text: A record made in three weeks in Allston, with the lineup changing underneath it. Brodsky ends up as the frontman, Caleb Scofield arrives on bass, and the van dies on a highway near Philadelphia.

years.h: Beyond Hypothermia gathers the 7-inches and early recordings
years.p: Wikipedia says the compilation gathers the earlier 7-inch releases and recordings, Cave In on tape before Brodsky became the singer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cave In · Wikipedia: Caleb Scofield
years.h: Scrod leaves two weeks before the debut session; Brodsky sings
years.p: With the first full-length two weeks away, Dave Scrod departs and Stephen Brodsky moves to lead vocals. [[Caleb Scofield|86aa5227-3afb-4198-bf58-9db0946e5d4b]] joins on bass after a try-out.
years.xp:
The band's bio, quoted on Wikipedia, says the surprise at Scofield's first rehearsal was that "he was a closet bass phenom." Scofield, from Pembroke, New Hampshire, had sung in a local hardcore band called Strike 3.

He would stay for twenty years, until his death in 2018.

years.cap: Recording at God City, Allston, with Kurt Ballou
years.h: Recorded in three weeks at God City with [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]]
years.p: Ballou, of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], engineers and co-produces the band's first full-length. Ballou, Jacob Bannon of Converge, Jay Randall of Agoraphobic Nosebleed and Travis Shettel of Piebald all add vocals.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes it as the first time the band recorded a complete album together, with two vocalists and one bassist cycling through the sessions. Adam McGrath has cited Cable, Rorschach and above all Converge as the influences; Brodsky has described it as worship of Converge.

years.h: Until Your Heart Stops · Hydra Head HH666-31
years.p: The debut full-length is a fast, dense metallic hardcore record, and the first with Brodsky at the microphone. Loudwire later put it on a list of the best metalcore albums.

years.cap: Cave In's Ford Econoline, before the fire
years.h: The van burns out 50 miles from Philadelphia
years.p: A tour with [[Isis|5e521e8c-0ab2-44c4-8fd8-14d8d3321265]] ends early when the band's 1991 Ford Econoline catches fire at a rest stop about fifty miles from Philadelphia. Wikipedia gives the location and vehicle.

eras.title: The Jupiter turn
eras.text: The band drops the screaming, looks up at the sky, and gets noticed by people with much bigger budgets. RCA calls.

years.h: Creative Eclipses EP points at the stars
years.p: The five-song EP is the first real sign of the band's move into space rock.

years.h: Jupiter · Hydra Head
years.p: Recorded in February and March 2000 with producer Brian McTernan, the album swaps most of the screaming for melody. "Big Riff" is the only song with screamed vocals.
years.xp:
The cover came in four colours across pressings: green first, then magenta, blue and yellow. Pitchfork gave it 4.9, Brave Words & Bloody Knuckles gave it 8 out of 10, and Decibel later ranked it the second-best metal album of the 2000s, per Wikipedia.

Wikipedia says Spin's Sound Advice column tagged the band "emo-metal Radiohead" around this time, a label the band rejected. Major labels started calling soon after.

years.cap: Cave In in the RCA years
years.h: Cave In signs to RCA Records
years.p: A band from Methuen with three Hydra Head records behind it takes a major-label deal in April 2001, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Antenna gets three months in Cello Studios, Los Angeles
years.p: Producer Rich Costey and RCA's money give the band three months to record, against four days for Jupiter. The whole process, per Wikipedia, ran six months.

years.h: Tides of Tomorrow, a six-song EP for Hydra Head
years.p: The band puts out a six-song EP on Hydra Head Records while on RCA, leaning further into melody.

eras.title: The major-label detour
eras.text: Three months in a Los Angeles studio, a Lollapalooza second stage, a European tour behind Foo Fighters and Muse, and a slow drift back toward the heavy music the band started with.

years.h: Antenna · RCA
years.p: The RCA debut is the band's biggest-sounding record: clean vocals, prog and space-rock textures. Alternative Press gave it five stars, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Adam McGrath told the story of the label years plainly: RCA tried harder to get things done, but more people wanted to put their fingerprints on the record. Executives pushed for radio-friendly singles, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Lollapalooza second stage, then Europe with Foo Fighters and Muse
years.p: The band plays the second stage of the 2003 Lollapalooza tour, then tours Europe supporting [[Foo Fighters|67f66c07-6e61-4026-ade5-7e782fad3a5d]] and Muse. The live shows start getting heavier again.

years.big: Backlash for growing out of it
q: We got major backlash for growing out of our metal phase.
years.h: Fans push back on the new sound
years.p: Longtime metal fans rejected the melodic direction of Antenna, Wikipedia reports.
years.xp: McGrath, quoted on Wikipedia, said the band got major backlash for growing out of its metal phase, and that he did not want those fans around.

years.src: Wikipedia: Perfect Pitch Black · Wikipedia: Antenna
years.h: RCA lets the band go over the heavier songs it recorded
years.p: Per Wikipedia, RCA and the band split in September 2004 after the label declined to release the heavier material the band had written. RCA returned ownership of those songs, and the band took them to Hydra Head.
years.xp: The Wikipedia pages for Antenna and Cave In differ on detail: one says the split followed a merger of RCA with BMG and Sony, another describes it as mutual after the tour. Both agree the band went back to Hydra Head with the songs.

eras.title: Heavy again, then quiet
eras.text: A record recorded over two years, a drummer who moves to Germany, and a hiatus that lasts until the band is ready to play in Allston again.

years.h: Perfect Pitch Black · Hydra Head
years.p: Recorded between January 2003 and April 2005 with Andrew Schneider, it is the band's return to slow, weird, heavy songs.
years.xp: Brodsky attributed the boogie feel to ZZ Top's Tejas on heavy rotation while touring, and the dueling guitars from the Allman Brothers.

years.h: Conners leaves for Germany; Ben Koller of Converge takes over drums
years.p: John-Robert Conners is injured and relocates to Germany, per Wikipedia. Ben Koller joins from [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] and plays the record's tours, including a cassette single of "Shapeshifter" and "Dead Already".

years.h: Cave In announces a hiatus
years.p: The band goes quiet after the touring for Perfect Pitch Black. Wikipedia dates the announcement to November 2006.

years.h: Brodsky and Conners form Pet Genius; Scofield starts Zozobra
years.p: Stephen Brodsky and John-Robert Conners release Pet Genius through Hydra Head. [[Caleb Scofield|86aa5227-3afb-4198-bf58-9db0946e5d4b]] begins [[Zozobra|a6b8ef30-1d47-4042-9b29-3963e4cd7a7a]], a sludge band that puts out Harmonic Tremors in 2007 and Bird of Prey in 2008, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Back at Great Scott's
eras.text: A reunion in Allston, two more Hydra Head records, and the odd one-off show, all with Scofield on bass.

years.h: Reunion at Great Scott's in Allston
years.p: The band announces the end of its three-year hiatus in April 2009 and plays its first show back, July 19, at Great Scott's in Allston. The new songs on the four-song Planets of Old EP debut that night.

years.h: Planets of Old, vinyl first, CD and DVD in 2010
years.p: Released first on vinyl by Hydra Head, then on CD in January 2010 with a DVD of the reunion show. "Retina Sees Rewind" and "Cayman Tongue" came out on iTunes.

years.h: White Silence, self-produced, art by Aaron Turner
years.p: The band produced the record itself; James Plotkin mastered it, and [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]] did the artwork. It charted at number 17 on Billboard's Top Heatseekers, per Wikipedia.

years.h: First show in three years: opening for Doomriders' tenth anniversary
years.p: After a stretch of undeclared hiatus, Cave In plays live for the first time in three years, opening for Doomriders' tenth anniversary show, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Brodsky's Mutoid Man releases Bleeder
years.p: Stephen Brodsky and [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] drummer Ben Koller's band [[Mutoid Man|d6c8e477-7221-47be-bab3-fe6980cf4284]], formed after Brodsky moved to New York City, puts out its debut LP.

eras.title: Losing Caleb
eras.text: The band's bassist for twenty years dies driving home from a writing weekend. The shows that follow are for his family.

years.h: Caleb Scofield dies in a crash at a New Hampshire toll plaza
years.p: Scofield, 39, died when his pickup struck a concrete barrier at the Bedford toll plaza on the Everett Turnpike, per Wikipedia and Spin. He was driving home from a writing and recording weekend with the band.
years.xp:
New Hampshire State Police, quoted by Spin, said he was trying to change lanes just before the plaza. Wikipedia cites the medical examiner as attributing his death to smoke and heat inhalation, thermal injuries and multiple blunt impact injuries. He left his wife and two children.

The band called him one of a kind and its best friend, per Spin. A crowdfunding page for his family passed its $1,000 goal quickly and raised around $72,000 within a day, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Benefit shows for Scofield's family
years.p: Cave In plays a Boston benefit on June 13 with [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], Young Widows and The Cancer Conspiracy; Caleb's brother Kyle and [[Nate Newton|5279c1b0-6751-4836-9c71-9abd227bd209]] cover the bass parts. A second benefit in Los Angeles, October 13, includes a one-off [[Isis|5e521e8c-0ab2-44c4-8fd8-14d8d3321265]] reunion.
years.xp: [[Old Man Gloom|75a97901-0051-4b67-a79b-9ebf2400d1d9]] shared bills with Cave In, and [[Stephen Brodsky|a0ff602c-7f3e-472d-8786-953da6cd7591]] stood in for Scofield there. Hydra Head issued a fundraising package of Zozobra reissues and unreleased tracks for the family, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Final Transmission
eras.text: Four-track demos become a record, a new bassist comes in, and a new label puts out the biggest-sounding Cave In record in twenty years.

years.h: Final Transmission · Hydra Head
years.p: Built from practice-space demos on a handheld four-track that include Scofield's bass, guitar and vocals on all nine tracks. Andrew Schneider mixed it; James Plotkin mastered it.
years.xp: Half of the album's proceeds went to Scofield's family. The opening track features a voice memo of Caleb pitching a song idea; Adam McGrath called it the end of the story of their relationship. The closer, Led to the Wolves, was largely composed by him.

years.h: The band records the vocals together on "Shake My Blood"
years.p: Brodsky said the song came from extreme grief, frustration and anger. Kerrang!'s Nick Ruskell called the album superb.

years.h: Cave In signs to Relapse Records
years.p: The band leaves the folded Hydra Head roster for Relapse, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Heavy Pendulum · Relapse
years.p: Recorded at [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]]'s GodCity in Salem, Massachusetts, it is the first Cave In album with [[Nate Newton|5279c1b0-6751-4836-9c71-9abd227bd209]] on bass. One riff is Scofield's, written in 2011.
years.xp: "Reckoning" is the first Cave In song written entirely by Adam McGrath. Four singles came ahead of the album. It reached number 2 on the UK Rock and Metal Albums chart, per Wikipedia.

years.h: McGrath's solo album Methuen's Lot
years.p: Adam McGrath releases the solo record, named for the town the band came from, per Wikipedia.
